evidence.title: A gateway out of room
evidence.body: 24% of requests fail at the gateway. Gateway CPU sits at 83%, and logins and checkouts both time out.

evidence.title: Gateway admission by lane
evidence.body: Lane observer-workload takes 4,200 requests a second, 61% of all admissions. Every other lane came in through a signed rollout. That one didn't.

evidence.title: Sessions that ask for nothing
evidence.body: Thousands of sessions a minute reuse the same few dozen session IDs, open, ask for nothing and close. None of them came in through a signed rollout.

evidence.title: One header on every repeat
evidence.body: Every repeating session carries the same header: x-session-tag: shadow-7.

evidence.title: No signature, no owner
evidence.body: The observer manifest is absent from the signed rollout ledger. Signature field blank, owner field blank, created 22 minutes ago by no pipeline.

evidence.title: Marcus's signature check
evidence.body: The signature matches no key Vantage has ever issued. Owner field blank. The workload is under a Security hold and must stay intact.

evidence.title: shadow-7 traced to the observer workload
evidence.body: Sessions tagged shadow-7 enter through admission lane observer-workload (pod observer-7f4c, namespace edge-canary) and hold 61% of gateway capacity.

evidence.title: Unregistered workload log fragment
evidence.body: UNKNOWN: you're looking at the wrong service.

beats.narrate: Three nights later, close to midnight. This time the pager doesn't bother with SEV2.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV1 · Request Gateway · request failure rate above 20%

beats.log: lane observer-workload · 4,200 req/s · 61% of admissions · signed rollout: none

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The gateway is drowning, and most of what's drowning it isn't customers. Tell me what it is before anyone touches it.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Logins and checkouts are both timing out. Customers say the app just thinks forever.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: There's a workload in edge-canary that nobody deployed through the pipeline. I've put a Security hold on it. Nobody deletes anything until I've looked.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: I read the pid 3318 postmortem, by the way. Tonight's thing smells the same.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Before I forget. The scheduler records I pulled for 3318 are gone. I didn't delete them.

beats.narrate: The pid 3318 line is still in your notes. Nobody has asked about it.

beats.log: 23:07:41.102 s-71c0 shadow-7 GET /session/open → 200, 0 bytes read
23:07:41.104 s-a93e - POST /checkout → 504 upstream timeout
23:07:41.105 s-71c0 shadow-7 GET /session/open → 200, 0 bytes read
23:07:41.109 s-0f22 - POST /login → 503 no capacity

beats.narrate: The same session opens again and again, milliseconds apart, and reads nothing. Every one of them wears the same tag.

options.text: Check edge-canary against the signed rollout ledger

beats.log: canary-web-14 · owner web-platform · signed release-key-2025b · run #58211 · 3 days ago
canary-auth-3 · owner identity · signed release-key-2025b · run #58190 · 4 days ago
observer-7f4c · owner (blank) · signed (blank) · run (none) · 22 minutes ago

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: It just got worse. A third of logins are failing.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Gateway log is full of one header. x-session-tag: shadow-7. Thousands of them.

options.text: Ask Marcus to check the workload's signature
options.consequence: Seventy-five seconds · Security owns that part

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Checking its signature against every key we've issued. Seventy-five seconds.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: While he looks — the gateway log is full of one header. x-session-tag: shadow-7.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Signature matches nothing we've ever issued. Not revoked, not expired, never ours. Owner field is blank. Fence it if you need to, but it stays intact. It's evidence now.

scenes.title: Where does it start?

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: No guesses. What on the board gives us a thread to pull?

scenes.prompt: The gateway can't tell this traffic from customers. Which two pieces of evidence lead you to where it starts?

hint.speaker: MAYA
hint.text: Not how bad it is, not who signed what. What marks these sessions, and which door do they come in by?

beats.narrate: Every shadow-7 session comes in on the one lane nobody signed for. Follow the tag down that lane and you reach whatever is sending it.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: That's a thread. Pull it.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Here's mine. They all wear shadow-7, and they all come in on the unsigned lane. Follow both.

beats.log: span 1 · request-gateway · admitted on lane observer-workload
span 2 · edge-canary/ingress · no client certificate presented
span 3 · edge-canary/observer-7f4c · origin; opens a new session every 3 ms
span 4 · (none) · no upstream caller

beats.narrate: The trace ends in a pod nobody claims. Nothing calls it. It just starts.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Checked it against the rollout ledger. No owner, no signature, no pipeline run. Created twenty-two minutes ago.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: That's the one under my hold. Fence it if you must. You don't touch it.

scenes.title: Your call

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Synthetic traffic just passed nine thousand a second. Whatever this is, it isn't slowing down on its own.

scenes.prompt: What do you do with the gateway?

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Out of time. I'm capping admissions.

options.text: Move the shadow-7 workload off customer capacity
options.consequence: Seventy-five seconds · Security keeps its evidence

beats.log: gateway: lane observer-workload → quarantine lane q-0

beats.narrate: Seventy-five seconds of watching the failure line while the gateway drains the lane.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Good. It's fenced into q-0 and it's still there. I can work with that.

options.text: Cap gateway admissions for two minutes
options.consequence: Holds the line · turns buyers away with the bots

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: The cap can't tell a bot from a buyer. One in six real checkouts is getting "too many requests".

beats.narrate: Two minutes later the cap expires.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: The cap expired and the workload never backed off. It queued everything we refused and sent it all at once.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Fence it. Now.

beats.log: gateway: lane observer-workload → quarantine lane q-0

options.consequence: Expensive · if it doesn't take the room first

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: It grew the moment we did. Synthetic rate doubled within a minute of the new nodes coming up. We're paying for its capacity.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Fence it. Now.

beats.log: gateway: lane observer-workload → quarantine lane q-0

options.consequence: Fastest if it works · Marcus has a hold on it

beats.speaker: ADMISSION
beats.text: delete deployment/observer-7f4c: denied. Policy SEC-HOLD: workload under Security investigation.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Who just tried to delete the observer? It's under my hold. We don't destroy the only evidence we have because it's inconvenient. Isolate it if you have to.

beats.narrate: Forty seconds gone, and the whole War Room knows who tried.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Fence it. Now.

beats.log: gateway: lane observer-workload → quarantine lane q-0

beats.narrate: The workload sits in q-0, still opening sessions to nobody. You open its manifest.

beats.log: kind: Deployment · name: observer-7f4c · namespace: edge-canary
owner: '' · signature: ''
replicas: auto (min 1, max unbounded) · session tag: shadow-7

beats.narrate: The manifest has every field a deployment needs except the two that say who sent it. At the bottom, where nobody puts anything, one comment line.

beats.log: # UNKNOWN: you're looking at the wrong service.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: No owner, no signature, and a comment addressed to whoever opened it. I'm logging the whole manifest. Nobody edit it.

scenes.title: Hand-off

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: I need the manifest and everything you pulled from it. Tonight.

scenes.prompt: What do you do with the manifest?

options.text: Hand everything to Marcus and keep nothing
options.consequence: By the book · it's Security's now

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Logged. If anyone asks you about observer-7f4c, send them to me.

options.text: Hand it over, and keep a private copy of the manifest
options.consequence: Behind Security's back · yours if it disappears

beats.narrate: observer-7f4c.yaml is two kilobytes. It fits on a drive nobody inventories.
It goes in the same folder as the pid 3318 line.
You think about Sam's scheduler records, gone by morning.

options.text: Post the comment line to the War Room, then hand it over
options.consequence: The team sees it · Marcus won't like it

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: "The wrong service." Great. Which one is the right one?

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Take that down. It's evidence, not a conversation.
